_meta.purpose: Visual biomechanics constraints for exercise image generation. Entries are gender-independent and keyed by ExerciseCatalog exercise id.
_meta.usage: Merge these constraints into the image prompt only when an exercise id exists here. ExerciseCatalog remains the source for general instructions/tips.

bodyPosition: hanging vertically from a pull-up bar
movement: vertical pull
elbows driven down toward the ribs

camera.priority: make the supinated grip and both palms visually unmistakable

bodyPosition: one or both forearms supported on the door frame
chest gently moving forward through the doorway
arms: upper arms around shoulder height or slightly below
movement: passive chest and anterior-shoulder stretch
torso advances forward while arm position remains supported

camera.priority: door frame contact and forward chest position must be obvious

bodyPosition: lying supine on a flat bench
movement: dumbbells press vertically above mid-chest

camera.priority: flat bench and two independent dumbbells clearly visible

mustNot: palms facing each other throughout like a fly

bodyPosition: lying supine on a clearly declined bench
legs secured by decline bench support
movement: dumbbells press upward from lower-chest line

camera.priority: the downward bench angle with head lower than hips must be unmistakable

hands: palms facing inward toward each other
movement: elbow flexion only
dumbbells travel toward shoulders without wrist rotation

camera.priority: neutral hammer grip must be clearly visible

bodyPosition: body aligned from head to heels
hands: both hands visibly lifted slightly off the floor beside the chest
movement: bottom of push-up with a deliberate hand release before pressing up

camera.priority: both hands must visibly lose contact with the floor

bodyPosition: standing centered between two cable columns
slight forward step or staggered stance
arms: hands meet or nearly meet in front of mid-chest
movement: horizontal adduction in a wide hugging arc

camera.priority: both chest-height cables and fly arc must be obvious

mustNot: cable press with strong elbow extension

bodyPosition: supported in a dedicated glute kickback machine
equipment: working foot pressing the machine platform or pad
movement: one leg drives backward and slightly upward through hip extension

camera.priority: dedicated machine and backward hip extension must be unmistakable

bodyPosition: standing centered between two low cable pulleys
equipment: two handles attached to pulleys at the lowest setting
arms: hands finish together in front of upper chest
movement: both handles travel diagonally upward and inward from low beside the hips toward upper chest

camera.priority: low pulley origin and upward diagonal cable path must be clearly visible

bodyPosition: seated upright in a hip abduction machine
equipment: outer thighs or knees pressing against the machine pads
movement: both knees move outward away from the body midline
legs visibly spread apart against resistance

camera.priority: OPEN leg position must be unmistakable

bodyPosition: seated upright in a hip adduction machine
equipment: inner thighs or knees pressing against the machine pads
movement: both knees move inward toward the body midline
legs finish close together against resistance

camera.priority: CLOSED leg position must be unmistakable

mustNot: legs spread wide at end range

movement: head gently follows a slow circular path
neck movement only

camera.priority: head tilt/rotation should communicate neck mobility without implying torso rotation

bodyPosition: upright running posture with slight natural forward lean
one leg in stance or push-off and the other advancing
environment: running path, track, road or park context
movement: natural running stride
elbows bent and arms driving front-to-back

camera.priority: clear running gait and outdoor setting

bodyPosition: standing or seated with torso hinged forward
arms: arms raised wide to the sides approximately in line with shoulders
movement: horizontal shoulder abduction driven by rear delts

camera.priority: hinged torso and wide lateral dumbbell path must be clear

bodyPosition: body suspended between parallel dip bars
movement: vertical bodyweight dip emphasizing elbow extension

camera.priority: parallel bars and suspended body must be obvious

mustNot: feet supporting body weight on floor

arms: both arms elevated overhead or sweeping through a controlled shoulder mobility arc
movement: bilateral shoulder mobility flow rather than loaded strength work

camera.priority: clearly communicate shoulder range-of-motion work

bodyPosition: arms extended out to sides for stability
movement: one leg bends and reaches across behind the body toward the opposite side
pelvis and lower torso rotate while shoulders remain relatively grounded

camera.priority: cross-body scorpion leg reach must be obvious

equipment: SkiErg with two independent overhead handles/cords
arms: handles being pulled down from overhead toward hips
movement: bilateral downward ski-pole pulling action coordinated with trunk and hip flexion

camera.priority: SkiErg tower, overhead cords and downward pull must all be recognizable

bodyPosition: lying supine on a flat bench centered inside a Smith machine
movement: bar travels on fixed rails toward and away from mid-chest

camera.priority: flat bench and Smith machine rails must be obvious

bodyPosition: lying on a decline bench inside a Smith machine
movement: guided bar lowers toward lower chest and presses upward

camera.priority: Smith rails plus clear head-lower-than-hips decline angle

bodyPosition: seated or standing directly under a Smith machine bar
arms: grip slightly wider than shoulder width
bar between shoulder level and overhead
movement: vertical guided overhead press

camera.priority: Smith rails and vertical overhead bar path must be visible

bodyPosition: legs kicked back into a strong plank-like position
movement: rapid transition from athletic standing/squat stance to hands-down legs-back position

camera.priority: hands-down legs-back sprawl position must be clear

mustNot: burpee jump as the focal phase
hips extremely high like downward dog

bodyPosition: hips above knees and kept relatively square
arms: working arm reaches under the torso across to the opposite side
back of working hand/arm near floor
movement: thoracic rotation with working shoulder and ear lowering toward floor

camera.priority: one arm visibly threaded underneath the torso

mustNot: both shoulders remaining square to floor

movement: bar lowers toward lower chest and presses upward

camera.priority: decline angle and barbell must both be unmistakable

bodyPosition: standing facing away from or slightly ahead of a low cable pulley
working upper arm positioned slightly behind torso
equipment: single low cable handle held in one hand
arms: working elbow remains behind or near torso
forearm curls forward/up while upper arm stays back
movement: unilateral elbow flexion from a lengthened behind-the-body biceps position

camera.priority: cable must originate behind the athlete and working upper arm must remain behind torso

bodyPosition: both feet fully on top of a sturdy plyometric box
knees and hips flexed in a soft partial-squat landing
movement: two-foot jump from floor onto top of box

camera.priority: both feet clearly landed on top surface of box

bodyPosition: standing facing a low cable machine
support leg planted with slight knee bend
torso mostly upright and pelvis square
equipment: ankle strap attached to the working ankle
cable attached at the lowest pulley setting
workingLeg: working leg extended backward and slightly upward behind the body
knee straight or only slightly bent
movement: hip extension backward, not sideways

camera.priority: ankle strap, low cable, and backward leg extension must all be clearly visible

bodyPosition: standing centered at a dual cable station
equipment: two cable handles or cable ends crossing in front of body
arms: arms opened wide approximately at shoulder height
movement: horizontal shoulder abduction, pulling cables outward and backward

camera.priority: cross-body cable setup and wide rear-delt opening must be obvious

mustNot: cable chest fly bringing hands together

bodyPosition: lying supine on a flat bench
movement: wide hugging arc around shoulder joint with minimal elbow-angle change

camera.priority: wide dumbbell fly arc must be clearly different from a dumbbell press

mustNot: bench press with elbows bending deeply

movement: symmetric jumping-jack open position with arms and legs moving laterally together

camera.priority: wide feet and overhead arms make the exercise instantly recognizable

bodyPosition: seated at a lat pulldown machine
equipment: wide pulldown bar attached to overhead cable
hands: pronated overhand grip wider than shoulder width
movement: bar pulled down in front of body toward upper chest
elbows driven downward

camera.priority: overhead cable, thigh pads, wide bar and bar-to-upper-chest position must be clear

movement: bar travels down close to thighs and shins through hip hinge
shins remain nearly vertical

camera.priority: hip hinge, nearly vertical shins and slight knee bend must distinguish it from a squat/deadlift

mustNot: bar starting from floor as conventional deadlift

bodyPosition: seated facing a low cable stack
equipment: cable handle pulled toward lower ribs
movement: horizontal pull with elbows traveling backward close to torso

camera.priority: low cable and lack of chest-support pad must distinguish it from a seated machine row

bodyPosition: seated upright with back and head against pec-deck seat
equipment: forearms or arms contacting padded levers/handles
movement: both machine arms close inward in front of chest

camera.priority: dedicated pec-deck machine must be unmistakable

bodyPosition: seated upright in a leg curl machine
equipment: padded lever positioned behind lower legs/ankles
movement: knees flex so lower legs curl downward and backward underneath the seat

camera.priority: seated posture, thigh restraint and downward/backward lower-leg curl must be obvious

bodyPosition: seated facing a dedicated row machine
chest firmly supported against a chest pad
equipment: dedicated seated row machine with handles
movement: handles pulled backward toward torso while chest remains on pad

camera.priority: chest-support pad and dedicated machine must distinguish it from a cable row

bodyPosition: standing side-on to a low cable machine
equipment: ankle strap attached to the working ankle
cable attached at the lowest pulley setting
workingLeg: working leg is the leg farther from the cable machine
working knee straight or only slightly bent
working leg visibly separated laterally from the support leg
movement: working leg moves laterally outward away from the body's midline
movement occurs primarily in the frontal plane

camera.priority: the outward movement and visible separation between the legs must be unmistakable

mustNot: working leg crossing in front of or behind the support leg
leg moving backward like a glute kickback

bodyPosition: standing sideways immediately next to a low cable machine
the cable machine is on the athlete's LEFT side
right leg is the stationary support leg
equipment: ankle strap attached to the LEFT ankle
LEFT ankle is the ankle closest to the cable machine
exactly one cable connects the LEFT ankle strap to the lowest pulley
workingLeg: LEFT leg is the working leg
LEFT leg starts beside the cable machine
LEFT leg moves RIGHTWARD toward the center of the athlete's body
LEFT leg passes in front of the stationary RIGHT leg
at end range the LEFT foot is slightly to the RIGHT of the body's center line
movement: the strapped LEFT leg moves FROM the cable-machine side TOWARD the opposite side
the distance between the strapped ankle and the cable machine INCREASES during the movement
the legs CLOSE together during the movement
the working leg crosses the body's center line

camera.priority: the LEFT strapped leg crossing inward in front of the stationary RIGHT leg must be unmistakable

mustNot: LEFT strapped leg moving left toward the cable machine
LEFT strapped leg moving outward away from the body's center line
working leg extending sideways away from the other leg
ankle strap on the RIGHT leg
